newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils close lower, rumour mill in overdrive.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils close lower, rumour mill in overdrive.

text.p: Rumours about China and Pakistan coupled with the volatile trading in Chicago kept most players sidelined on the European vegetable oil market on Tuesday.
Traders said the rumour mill had gone into over drive with talk of a default by China and rumours of problems with a sunflower oil shipment to Pakistan.
Rumours that China had defaulted on shipment on a Mar/May shipment of palm oil drove prices down towards the close of the Malaysian market Tuesday.
However, European traders said they could not track the rumour down.
"We can't find any confirmation of this. But when people who are normally connected with Chinese business are seen in the market rumours always start about China buying or defaulting," said one.

There was also talk that a 30,000 tonnes shipment of sunflower oil to Pakistan was being sold in road tanker loads at a discount to palm oil on the local market because a letter of credit had not be honoured.
"Like the China rumour we can't get to the bottom of this one, but if it's true someone, somewhere won't be getting much sleep," said one trader.
Volatile trading in Chicago was another factor keeping a lid on business.
